newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican stocks end lacklustre day slightly higher.
newsitem.headline: Mexican stocks end lacklustre day slightly higher.

text.p: Mexican share prices ended slightly higher in a dull session on Monday marked by thin trade due to the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
"There was very little action, although a few of the infrastructure stocks did well following (President Ernesto Zeidllo's) state of the nation address (on Sunday)," one dealer at Probursa said.
The bourse's leading IPC index ended up 4.11 points, or 0.12 percent, to 3,309.58.
Volume was a razor-thin 15.24 million shares.

Builder Tribasa led the day's gainers, gaining 3.21 percent. Analysts said Tribasa, which is big on toll road concessions, was helped by Zedillo's comments during his address that the government planned to spend some 0.6 percent of GDP -- about 14 billion pesos -- in restructuring toll road debt.

"We had recommended Tribasa shares a few weeks ago because it was at a good price and because the construction sector is looking better," said Francisco Blanco, director of analysis at Arka brokerage firm.
He said he thought Tribasa shares had further upside.
There were 31 gainers and 24 losers on the big board.
Market heavyweight Telmex L shares slipped 0.16 percent.
-- Maria Luisa Aguilar, Mexico City newsroom 525 7289565
